title: Leading Through Incidents and Change: Capstone Workshop
summary: Brings the programme together in a simulated incident and change scenario, followed by a personal leadership plan covering direction for the team, accountability and continuing development.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: Brings the programme together in a simulated incident and change scenario, followed by a personal leadership plan covering direction for the team, accountability and continuing development.
Learning Objectives: Lead a team through a time-pressured incident and communicate decisions clearly
Plan and sustain change in the function's structure, tools or approach
Produce a personal leadership development plan
Syllabus: Decision-making under pressure: bias, incomplete information and ownership
Leading change: new regulation, restructuring and technology in the second line
Simulation: a breach escalating to the board and the supervisor
Workshop: the twelve-month personal leadership plan
Intended Audience: Compliance, risk and financial crime specialists newly promoted, or preparing for promotion, into team leader and manager roles
Heads of compliance, chief risk officers, MLROs and their deputies seeking to strengthen how they lead and position the function
Senior managers who lead other control or assurance teams, or who sponsor the second line within the business
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience in a compliance, risk or financial crime role is helpful. No prior management training is required.
Core Reading: Amy C. Edmondson, The Fearless Organization: Creating Psychological Safety in the Workplace (2018)
Patrick Lencioni, The Five Dysfunctions of a Team (2002)
IOSCO, Compliance Function at Market Intermediaries (2006)
FSB, Strengthening Governance Frameworks to Mitigate Misconduct Risk: A Toolkit for Firms and Supervisors (2018)
